values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Weston Wildlife Conservation Site: one parking area at the end of the gravel access road; no restroom or trash disposal.

booking.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ + https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/weston/ (Facilities: 'The parking area is located at the end of the WCS access road ... Primitive camping is allowed. No restroom or trash disposal facilities are available.'; Maps & Directions: 'Follow gravel road to the left to access the parking area.'), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Weston page that primitive camping is still allowed ('Primitive camping is allowed'; listed under Recreational Opportunities) with one parking area at the end of a gravel access road and no restroom or trash; statewide page: no hookups/water/dump, 14-night limit, $10 authorization. No designated campsites, so ownership wma stands. Not stated: season, RV suitability of the access road, phone. Note (with the $10 / $4 Access Permit line) left as is.
flags: Name: DWR's page now calls the property the 'Weston Wildlife Conservation Site (WCS)' (271 acres, 'owned by the Department since 1959'); the entry says 'Weston Wildlife Management Area' (https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/weston/). Consider renaming.

Info: Weston is designated 'Chase Only' for beagle and bird-dog training, September 1 - March 31, daylight hours (https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/weston/): expect dog-training activity in season. Turkey Run (creek, 8-25 ft wide) is the only water; the entry's not-waterfront value is consistent with the page.
